verdicts.means: The area meets every part of the pass rule.
The area misses the pass rule but meets every part of the near rule.
The known inputs miss both rules, whatever the value of an unknown input.
An input that can change the verdict is unknown.

notes: The rules never count an unknown input as a fail.
The page rounds each input as it prints it. Then it applies the rule.
C and T are means over the three periods. Each period uses the value of the month of its middle day.
H30 counts only hours inside spells of at least 2 hours with the Sun in the band.
The three periods can continue past the end of the year.
If the snow maps are doubtful, the rules use the lower and more cautious snow-free odds.
Snow is not measured in Antarctica. Thus, S is unknown there.
In that case, a rule that needs S gives 'cannot tell', unless the known inputs decide the verdict.
In Antarctica K is the share of all low-Sun hours in those periods that the terrain leaves.
C counts cloud over all hours of the month. Thus, it tells too little about a Sun this low.
T is a model mean over all hours and a wide grid box, not the air during the low-Sun hours.
In Antarctica H30 counts the rock season only, 27 November to 1 March, with terrain but without snow.
If no airfield of that kind is within 1,500 km, D counts as more than 1,500 km.
